title: How Jacky Chou built niche sites, e-commerce and an SEO agency into a diversified online portfolio
summary: Jacky Chou walks through his path from electrical engineering to SEO, a Drop Shipping win that crashed, and launching Far and Away via Kickstarter. He covers Facebook ads, conversion fixes, why e-commerce stores should add affiliate and display revenue, and how niche sites, agencies and e-commerce balance each other.

principles.text: Launch a physical product on Kickstarter to validate demand with little cash and no factory minimums.
principles.quote: all you have to do is go to the factory shoot some beautiful uh videos and imagery and launch on Kickstarter

principles.text: Facebook ads: test many creatives, nail targeting, and burn budget early to mature the pixel.
principles.quote: the key to Facebook ads is one test a lot of different creatives to uh the proper targeting and three is uh maturing your pixel

principles.text: When ads get clicks but no sales, the website's conversion rate optimization is usually the problem.
principles.quote: nine times out of ten uh the websites of the businesses I've taken to look at are absolute garbage and they don't they they don't have proper uh cro in place

principles.text: Add affiliate and display revenue to e-commerce stores, since thin net margins make core growth hard to fund.
principles.quote: I believe all Ecommerce stores should open up different channels of Revenue or revenue streams and that would include display ads and affiliate Revenue as well

principles.text: Require very high gross margins on e-commerce products so ads and shipping don't erase profit.
principles.quote: it's got to be like 70 80 plus gross margins

principles.text: Pair slow-ramping niche sites with an agency for cash flow, so one business going to zero doesn't sink you.
principles.quote: agencies are great for cash flow uh pretty decently high margin business and extremely low risk
